$description: Locked shell/navigation rules per role and surface. Derived from ux/WEB_UX.md, ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md, ux/SCREEN_UX_SPECS.md §10, design-system/COMPONENTS.md § Navigation. This file is what a generic AppShell mapping must consult BEFORE assuming every authenticated route gets the same shell — Course Player is the one locked exception.

publicWeb.appliesTo: Guest, every unauthenticated route (Landing, Explore (public), Course Details (public), Learning Paths (public), Login, Register)
publicWeb.lockedRule: No language-toggle control in this Navbar — language selection lives only in Settings (post-auth) and is reached the same way by Guest per ux/WEB_UX.md § 5 (a guest-accessible Settings-equivalent is NOT implemented — this is a known, disclosed scope boundary of the current implementation, not a design-to-code decision).

authenticatedStudent.appliesTo: Student role, all /app/* routes EXCEPT Course Player and Quiz (see coursePlayerShell below)
authenticatedStudent.itemsStructuredSource: web/src/components/navigation/app-shell.tsx NAV_ITEMS (implementation evidence) — now the generation SOURCE; app-shell.tsx consumes the generated constant instead of hand-defining this array (see design-to-code/validation/MAPPING_REPORT.md)

topBar.height: component-specific, see web implementation for the exact px value — not separately tokenized as its own component in COMPONENTS.md

coursePlayerShell.$description: LOCKED RULE — the single most important navigation exception in the product. Do NOT let a generic AppShell mapping override this.
coursePlayerShell.name: Focused Learning Shell
coursePlayerShell.rule: The normal authenticated Sidebar COLLAPSES to its 72px icon-only state while these screens are active — this is a COLLAPSE, not a full removal, and not a distinct second shell component. ux/SCREEN_UX_SPECS.md § 10: 'Web — reduced-chrome (Sidebar collapsed by default), a slim top bar with course title + close/back affordance.'
coursePlayerShell.mechanism: A React Context (SidebarForceCollapseContext in the current web implementation) that the Course Player/Quiz screen sets on mount and clears on unmount — NOT a route-level shell swap.

content: course title + "Lesson N of M · X% complete"
topBar.replaces: the normal Sidebar top bar's hamburger+username row while this screen is active

coursePlayerShell.showcaseDeviationNote: The locked showcase's own caption over-states this as 'the one documented exception to authenticated sidebar navigation,' which could be misread as 'no sidebar at all.' The authoritative source (ux/SCREEN_UX_SPECS.md § 10, 'Sidebar collapsed by default') says collapsed, not removed — rank 1 (UX) wins per SOURCE_MANIFEST.json precedence. This conflict is recorded, not silently resolved.

mobileStudentShell.$description: LOCKED — Android/iOS bottom-tab shell, the Student-only mobile counterpart to Web's authenticatedStudent Sidebar. Added at Phase 4 Task 3 (design-to-code/screens/mobile-*.json extraction pass) from the showcase's real MobileBottomNavigation component (§ 17) plus rank-1 product/UX confirmation of the exact item set/order — this shell did NOT exist in this file before Task 3; see design-to-code/shared/platform-contract.json#/android/readinessNotes, updated in the same pass to point here instead of calling it 'not-yet-specified.'
mobileStudentShell.appliesTo: Student role, mobile app (Android & iOS — ux/MOBILE_UX.md: 'Android and iOS share this exact UX specification'), all 5 tab-root screens and every pushed/nested screen except Course Player and Quiz (see hiddenOn below)
mobileStudentShell.itemsStructuredSource: ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1, product/INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md § 3, ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md § 3 — the exact 5-item set/order/labels are a rank-1 product/UX lock, NOT read from the showcase (see labelConflict below for why the showcase's own assembled preview frames are not the source of truth for item 3's English label).
mobileStudentShell.badges: none in MVP — no unread-count/notification badge (ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1; product/MVP_SCOPE.md: Mentora has no notification system in MVP).
mobileStudentShell.tapActiveTabBehavior: Tapping the active tab's own icon while already at that tab's root pops that tab's stack back to root (ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1).
mobileStudentShell.backStacks: Each of the 5 tabs owns an independent push/pop stack; switching tabs never pushes onto another tab's stack, and each tab remembers its own stack position on return (ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md § 3).

hiddenOn.rule: The bottom nav is FULLY HIDDEN (not merely reduced) on Course Player and Quiz — ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1: '...Course Player and Quiz hide it...'; ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 8 confirms for Quiz specifically ('Full-screen, bottom nav hidden').
hiddenOn.platformDifferenceFromWeb: DISCLOSED PLATFORM DIFFERENCE, not a visual-identity divergence: Web's equivalent focused-learning-shell rule (this file's own coursePlayerShell, above) COLLAPSES the Sidebar to a 72px icon-only rail — it is never fully removed. Mobile's bottom nav has no partial/collapsed state to fall back to at mobile width; it is fully hidden on these two screens instead. Sanctioned as a platform-appropriate (not identity) difference by design-system/DESIGN_RULES.md rule 10, restated in ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 15. A generic cross-platform shell mapping must not assume mobile 'collapses' the way Web does.

mobileStudentShell.visibleOn: Every other authenticated Student screen keeps the bottom nav visible, including screens that are 'browsing, not doing' per ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1 (Course Details, My Learning's course list, Certificates, Settings) — do not hide it there by analogy with Web's Sidebar-collapse screens.

visualValues.height: 64dp + safe-area inset (design-review-locked/Mentora Showcase.dc.html § 17, line 1505: 'height:64px' — the safe-area addition is a native-platform concern with no 2D-mockup equivalent, per shared/components.json#/mobileBottomNavigation, rank 2)
visualValues.border: border.width.default color.border.default, top edge only (Showcase § 17, line 1505: border-top:1px solid var(--bd))
visualValues.icon: 24dp (Showcase § 17: every nav icon rendered at font-size:24px)
visualValues.label: typography.caption (Showcase § 17: font:400 12px/16px Inter, letter-spacing 0.4px — an exact byte match to shared/typography.json#/caption)
visualValues.activeColor: brand.primary (Showcase § 17, line 1506: color:var(--brand) on the active item)
visualValues.inactiveColor: text.secondary (Showcase § 17, lines 1507-1510: color:var(--txt2) on every non-active item)
visualValues.verifiedSourceLines: design-review-locked/Mentora Showcase.dc.html § 17 Navigation, 'SIDEBAR COLLAPSED · 72 · AND MOBILE BOTTOM NAVIGATION' sub-block (lines 1493-1533, re-verified by direct read — not the Phase 4 plan's approximate citation). The LTR nav row itself is lines 1504-1512; the RTL nav row is lines 1513-1521.

rtlMirroring.note: Same visual left-to-right icon/label order is kept and simply read right-to-left as a whole (the row's internal item order never reverses) — consistent with this file's rtlMirroring convention for every other nav surface.
rtlMirroring.verifiedSourceLines: design-review-locked/Mentora Showcase.dc.html § 17, lines 1513-1521 (real Arabic labels, verified by direct read).

labelConflict.description: Showcase-internal inconsistency, confined to the English label and verified by direct read of every occurrence: § 17's own dedicated MobileBottomNavigation component block (lines 1504-1521, both the LTR and RTL rows) already correctly labels item 3 'My Learning' / 'مساحة التعلّم' — it does not disagree with rank-1. The actual disagreement is between § 17 on one side, and §§ 20/22's assembled MOBILE PREVIEW illustration frames on the other: every English bottom-nav row inside those frames (§ 20 'MOBILE · 360', line 1864; § 22's Home/Explore/My Learning/Home-Dark-Mode frames, lines 2063, 2109, 2191, 2403) labels item 3 the single word 'Learning' — including, ironically, inside the My Learning screen's own frame (line 2191, page title 'My Learning' at line 2162 but its own active nav label reads 'Learning'). The Arabic label is unaffected: § 22's Home · Arabic RTL frame (line 2366) uses the same correct 'مساحة التعلّم' as § 17 — the inconsistency is English-microcopy-only in the illustration frames, not a second locked value or a translation disagreement.
labelConflict.resolution: Resolved to 'My Learning' per design-to-code/SOURCE_MANIFEST.json's rank-1-over-rank-3 precedence: ux/MOBILE_UX.md § 1, product/INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md § 3, and ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md § 3 all lock 'My Learning', and § 17's own dedicated component spec already agrees with rank-1. §§ 20/22's shorter 'Learning' is treated as illustration-frame shorthand, never adopted. Every mobile-*.json screen spec and this shell entry use 'My Learning'.

instructorWeb.itemsStructuredSource: web/src/components/navigation/instructor-shell.tsx INSTRUCTOR_NAV_ITEMS (implementation evidence) — now the generation SOURCE.
instructorWeb.note: Course/Lesson/Quiz Editor are reached by drilling into a course from the Dashboard's course list, not via top-level Sidebar items.

adminWeb.itemsStructuredSource: web/src/components/navigation/admin-shell.tsx ADMIN_NAV_ITEMS (implementation evidence) — now the generation SOURCE, same pattern as instructorWeb.
adminWeb.note: Per ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md § 5, Admin's own Profile/Settings are intentionally not top-level sidebar items here (exactly like instructorWeb's flow table never lists them either) — Task 12's explicit scope is Dashboard/Courses/Users/Instructors/Categories only; Logout remains reachable via AppShell's always-present sidebar-footer action regardless of navItems.

mirrors: Sidebar position (moves to end/right edge in RTL)

neverMirrors.$description: The one locked, product-wide exception list.
neverMirrors.videoPlayerScrubber: Course Player's VideoPlayer scrubber/timeline always renders LTR regardless of app layout direction (design-system/COMPONENTS.md § Media & Playback, design-system/LOCALIZATION.md § 2-3).
neverMirrors.icons: icon.directional.neverMirror list (play/pause, check, cancel, search, add, remove, drag_indicator, more_vert, etc.) — non-directional glyphs never flip.
neverMirrors.certificateContent: Certificate Detail's own rendered content (name, course title) follows the certificate's authored language direction, which may be LTR regardless of current app UI direction — a narrow, deliberate exception similar in spirit to the VideoPlayer rule.
neverMirrors.numerals: Total/price amounts always render as Western Arabic numerals regardless of locale (design-system/LOCALIZATION.md § 7).

backNavigationRules.purchaseSuccess: Browser/system back is redirected to My Learning rather than re-entering the completed checkout (ux/NAVIGATION_SPEC.md § 6).
